prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website visual direction comp, 16:10 landscape, first viewport plus a small glimpse below
Primary request: Design an award-caliber 2026 personal portfolio homepage for Daniel Vieira Teixeira, a full-stack software engineer. Visual world: an interactive variable-font specimen where typography demonstrates engineering adaptability as the problem changes.
Structure: near-invisible top navigation with Daniel's small name and Biography / Experience / Contact. One enormous phrase fills most of the viewport: One problem. Many modes. with letters shifting dramatically from narrow/light to wide/heavy across the line. A precise vertical axis control at right moves through FRONTEND / BACKEND / QA / RELIABILITY and shows compact live labels such as MODE 03 and WEIGHT 740. Beneath the display phrase, a concise offer explains the value and a sharp START A PROJECT action anchors the lower-right. A small edge of a four-mode project index appears below.
Style/medium: real polished website UI, contemporary foundry specimen meets engineering interface, radical type scale, rigorous baseline grid, flat semantic controls, crisp registration marks, no decorative imagery, no generic cards.
Color palette: near-white #F4F1EA dominant ground, ink black #141414, electric ultramarine #315CFF as the only strong accent.
Materials/textures: type proofs, axis readouts, registration marks, flat uncoated stock feeling without photorealistic paper.
Text (verbatim): Daniel Vieira Teixeira; One problem. Many modes.; I move across frontend, backend, QA, and reliability to find the right intervention.; FRONTEND; BACKEND; QA; RELIABILITY; START A PROJECT; Cape Town, South Africa.
Constraints: the engineering offer must be clear within seconds. Avoid invented clients, metrics, logos, awards, testimonials, stock photos, gradients, glassmorphism, dark neon, terminal aesthetics, rounded SaaS cards, mock browser chrome, watermarks. Must read as a functioning portfolio homepage, not a typography poster.
